title: First-class MU/MI estate controller boundary
summary: The dev14 generic controller makes MU and MI native ooRexx estate objects, publishes read-only estate service operations, and preserves authority separation; ED209 must extend that object model to ten MUs/twenty MIs without turning the controller into a scheduler.
invariants: RexxOSGridEstateController owns Grid identity, membership and observations; it does not own placement, ACTIVE/SPARE choice, Storage residency, Memory allocation, XTP route choice, economics, cloud purchase, transport selection or serialization selection.
RexxOSManagementUnitController is a first-class MU controller. Its subordinate MI membership is explicit; an MU is not inferred from MI rows.
RexxOSGridEstateMember preserves semantic member identity and incarnation. Advice or observations fenced to an old incarnation must fail closed after replacement.
The dev14 service endpoint is read-only through RpcServiceCore; ConnectSelector chooses DirectCall/RPC/Queue and the binding/SerializationSelector owns encoding.
Instrumentation may publish Grid and per-MU observations but never acquires mutation authority.
procedure: Extend the generic controller commissioning adapter with the ten current ED209 MU identities and twenty MI memberships.
Preserve exact MU/MI incarnations across restart and reject stale advice, placement or movement evidence after membership-generation change.
Keep field carrier commissioning outside the controller domain model; expose observed route evidence rather than carrier policy mutation.
